Walking directions

    ABOUT THE DATA

    Useful context. Honest limits.

    See where the information comes from, how comparisons work, and what remains unknown.

    Partial public data

    Confidential and juvenile reports are withheld. Homicide is undercounted; rape and sexual-offense reports can also be missing. Other categories are not included. Read the source limitations ↗

    How blocks and report counts work

    In live mode, shapes use official 2020 Census blocks, clipped to the SF shoreline. They generally follow streets; parks, large sites and changed streets can differ. Only boundary geometry is used.

    Each block includes selected reports at published intersections inside or within 35 m of it. Reports can appear beside multiple blocks. Selecting several areas produces a unique combined total on the server; adding individual counts would double-count shared reports. Masked locations cannot identify a building or exact event location. Longer report windows naturally contain more reports.

    Route overlap estimates distance inside or within 15 m of the darkest blocks, including shared street edges. A reduction must also hold with a 50 m margin. These are display and comparison choices, not validated danger boundaries or a safety model.

    What this directory covers

    Current public housing is listed by SFHA. Former public housing includes converted properties and completed replacement phases identified in the City housing portfolio. These labels describe the development, not every unit.

    Reentry housing includes publicly listed residential programs with verified addresses; it is a broader category than halfway houses. Offices, confidential residences, planned sites and unresolved addresses are excluded. Some programs and parts of large developments are missing.

    City housing records were updated May 21, 2026; sources were reviewed October 8. Each pin links to its evidence. This is a reviewed snapshot, not a live occupancy feed or a complete inventory. Listings are withheld after their review deadline.

    Saving and opening directions

    Saved trips stay in this browser on this device. They do not sync to another phone or computer. You can remove them at any time.

    Live saves retain only the addresses and handoff stops you entered, your preferences, and the evidence date you reviewed. They do not retain the selected route or directions: the current Mapbox Navigation terms prohibit storing or exporting those results. Reopening a trip asks you to confirm addresses and compare current routes again. The fictional sample can preserve its invented route.

    Apple and Google Maps receive your entered start, destination and optional ordered stops, with San Francisco added when needed, only when you open their link. They calculate their own walking route, which can use streets you avoided here. Some app versions may ignore stops. Check the matched addresses, stop order and streets before starting. Stops are never automatically copied from Mapbox output and do not alter the comparison here. New Apple walking links require a supported version of Maps; browser and app behavior can differ.

    Directions are planning information, without live location tracking, voice guidance or automatic rerouting. Observe signs, closures and actual conditions.

    FICTIONAL

    Evidence coverage

    We cannot assess current lighting, construction, sidewalk access, crowd levels, or changes made since these records.

    How sensitive are these counts?

    Change the screening corridor. Nearby records can enter or leave the count; this is not a measure of risk.

    A CLEARER WAY TO CHOOSE

    Useful context. Honest limits.

    01 / ROUTES

    Start with a real choice.

    Compare available walking options against your detour limit. An alternative is never guaranteed.

    02 / EVIDENCE

    Keep the concerns separate.

    Pedestrian collision history and reported incidents answer different questions. We never blend them into a safety score.

    03 / JUDGMENT

    Leave the decision with you.

    Fewer reports do not establish lower risk. Facility markers describe the place type; they do not label residents or imply danger. When evidence cannot support a comparison, we say so.

    BUILT TO BE QUESTIONED

    Open about our evidence.

    The sample walk uses invented records. The local live preview uses historical crash and police snapshots when configured. Live routes also include a small reviewed facility directory with partial coverage. HIN, dispatch and 311 layers are not connected.

    A TRANSPARENT PROTOTYPE

    This is a fictional sample walk.

    Every route shape, duration, facility location, collision, and incident in Sample walk mode is illustrative. Real addresses anchor the example, but the map is schematic and cannot be used for navigation.

    The demo evaluates invented points against invented route lines using the same deterministic rules covered by our tests. It demonstrates trade-offs, missing coverage, stale data, and sensitivity to distance thresholds.

    Live routing requires a Mapbox token and the local server. Live routes never receive fictional evidence. Real SF evidence ingestion and validation remain a separate launch gate.
